text:
incident-bot: ALERT: GeoDNS inconsistency detected for api.redwood.ai starting 2025-05-10 15:20 UTC. Elevated NXDOMAINs observed from several external resolvers in eu and ap regions. Pager triggered to oncall.
Maya: got the page — looking into DNS graphs now.
Maya: seeing spike in NXDOMAIN + 5xx from eu-west and ap-south. Service error rate up ~8-12% for generation endpoint, retries succeed for a chunk.
Liam: Observed mismatch between Route53 and Cloudflare authoritative answers. Route53 returns the expected CNAME chain; CF edge returns a stale/removed record in some regions. dig snippet below.
```bash
; <<>> DiG 9.11.3 <<>> api.redwood.ai @8.8.8.8
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: NXDOMAIN, id: 12345
;; flags: qr rd ra; QUERY: 1, ANSWER: 0
```
Ravi: Ravi K. (primary oncall) — taking. Any recent DNS or infra changes?
Sara: No infra deploys in the last 3 hours. We did a delegation update in Route53 earlier this week (small change).
Jen: Support seeing customer tickets from EU complaining about 502/timeout patterns. Two high-priority reports so far.
Maya: Hypothesis: external cache divergence after delegation update leading to inconsistent resolver views -> some resolvers returning NX. Mitigation options: 1) Flip GeoDNS policy to prefer the provider with consistent answers in impacted AZs, 2) push temporary override on our GeoDNS control plane, 3) engage Cloudflare to flush/inspect their edge caches.
Liam: I can push a geo-priority flip to prefer Route53 for eu & ap regions. That should make affected resolvers get the consistent answers quickly (prop time depends on TTL). Prep rollback plan first.
Ravi: Go ahead. Document the change and rollback steps. Maya, draft the status page blurb.
Maya: Drafting: "We are investigating an elevated error rate for api.redwood.ai affecting a subset of EU and APAC customers due to inconsistent DNS answers between external providers. Engineers are mitigating by routing affected traffic to a consistent DNS provider; retries are likely to succeed. We will update within 30 minutes." Post?
Maya: Posted status update to status.redwood.ai/incidents/2025-05-10 :white_check_mark:
deploy-bot: Deploy job 48231 queued: config.flip.geo-priority -> route53-pref (triggered by Liam).
Liam: executing flip now. Command: 
```bash
redwoodctl dns set-geopolicy --domain api.redwood.ai --priority route53 --scope eu,ap
```
Liam: applying canary to eu-west.
incident-bot: ACTION: GeoDNS policy changed by Liam at 2025-05-10T15:29:02Z — canary to eu-west.
Maya: Monitoring metrics... NXDOMAIN rate in eu-west dropping, visible improvement.
Jen: Confirmed fewer customer error reports coming in.
Ravi: Monitor for 15 mins, then expand if stable.
Liam: expanding to ap-south and ap-northeast now.
incident-bot: ACTION: GeoDNS policy expanded to ap-south, ap-northeast at 2025-05-10T15:34:20Z.
Maya: After expansion global NXDOMAIN and 5xx rates are back close to baseline; latency normalizing. Leaving canary for 1h then start post-incident review.
Sara: Created incident doc: /docs/incidents/1752500000-dns-geo-sync-lag.md. Assigned postmortem owner: Liam.
Ravi: Handoff plan: I'll own mitigation until 16:30 UTC, then hand to Maya for follow-up and postmortem.
Liam: I'll open a case with Cloudflare support (ticket CF-59231) to request root-cause for stale edge responses and confirm TTL propagation semantics.
Maya: Next steps: 1) Full postmortem with timeline, dig outputs, TTLs, delegation history. 2) Customer outreach for most impacted accounts. 3) Add an automated monitor comparing authoritative answers across providers.
Jen: Preparing customer outreach draft and list of affected accounts.
incident-bot: INCIDENT severity reduced and page closed at 2025-05-10T15:45:00Z. Mitigation in place; follow-ups required.
Ravi: Closing thread; notes in incident doc. Thanks everyone for quick response.
